newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab women prisoners say freedom tastes bittersweet.
newsitem.headline: Arab women prisoners say freedom tastes bittersweet.

text.p: Suad al-Jubeh, released from an Israeli prison after five years, said freedom tasted bittersweet.
The 23-year-old East Jerusalem resident held her mother in a long embrace late on Tuesday in her first homecoming since being sentenced in 1992 to nine years in jail for stabbing a Jewish settler.
Prison authorities released Jubeh and 30 other Palestinian women under peace deals with the PLO. Thousands of other Palestinians remain behind bars.

"I feel it is an incomplete peace. They were supposed to release all of the prisoners but they have not released them all. Many of our brothers are still in jail in difficult conditions," Jubeh told Reuters at her grandparents' home.
Jubeh's seven brothers lined up to kiss her in an emotional but tearless reunion. Her mother, Amra, said Jubeh sustained a head injury in jail while being beaten by prison authorities.

Jubeh was a member of the militant Islamic Jihad group -- which has opposed Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule authority -- when she stabbed the Jewish settler in Jerusalem's Old City. She now supports Arafat.
She travelled first to Ramallah in the West Bank for a meeting with the Palestinian president before continuing to East Jerusalem.
Arafat hugged and kissed the women as they arrived in Ramallah hours after their release.

Jubeh was among the first women prisoners to be freed on Tuesday. A petition to the High Court after she was let out held up the release of nine women for hours while others refused to leave until all 31 were freed.
"We did not know that the rest were not released when we left," said Aisha Abu Hazem, another woman prisoner released before the petition.
Hazem, sentenced in 1995 to 12 years in prison for stabbing an Israeli soldier, said all women were compelled to sign commitments to refrain from violence.

"I don't feel happy since many prisoners are still in jail. I'm also sad that Lamya has been deported," she said, referring to Lamya Maarouf, a 32-year-old Brazilian citizen released on Tuesday and deported to Brazil.
"She had no choice except to stay in jail and appeal or to be deported. They promised her she would return soon," Hazem told Reuters.
